benefits.title: Students can recognise, shape and carry forward the full value of their learning
benefits.statement: Students develop a detailed and evidence-informed understanding of the capabilities they build through their course and wider King’s experience. They can connect those capabilities with their purposes, identify what they want to develop and communicate their distinctive value with greater confidence without needing a fixed occupational destination.
benefits.successLooksLike: Students can explain capabilities they have developed, distinguish claim from evidence and assurance, understand relevance across different contexts and futures and make informed choices about further development.

benefits.title: Disciplinary capabilities become visible within a shared institutional language
benefits.statement: Programme teams and faculties can surface distinctive combinations of disciplinary, higher-order and transferable capabilities without having to fit them into a narrow generic attribute set or create isolated local frameworks.
benefits.successLooksLike: Trailblazer programmes can describe characteristic capabilities within a common architecture, make them visible to students and use them to support meaningful conversations about curriculum, learning design and development; the elements selected for wider use have evidence of portability beyond the trailblazers.

benefits.title: King’s can connect education, opportunity and student futures more coherently
benefits.statement: A shared skills language connects student purpose, curriculum, wider opportunities, evidence, recognition, microcredentials and graduate articulation. It provides a stronger basis for engagement with external audiences while preserving individual and disciplinary diversity.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, King’s, employers and external partners
benefits.successLooksLike: Skills information can be used coherently across the student journey and understood beyond King’s, with the institutional architecture drawing on evidence from discovery and trailblazer practice rather than generic claims.

benefits.title: King’s contributes a credible higher education response to the national skills agenda
benefits.statement: By testing the UK Standard Skills Classification rigorously rather than adopting it symbolically, King’s can contribute practical evidence about how a detailed national skills language can or cannot strengthen degree-level education while preserving academic breadth and disciplinary integrity.
benefits.beneficiary: King’s, students, the higher education sector, government and employers
benefits.successLooksLike: King’s is recognised as a credible partner whose practical evidence informs the application or development of a national skills language, including transparent learning about limitations, required adaptations and contexts where the approach does not add value.
